encoder: ChatGPT, outside Legalese's pipeline skill (an external contribution)
contributed_by: michaellegalese, commit d7983848 on main, 2026-09-22 (originally under subjects/israel/hvac_l4)
display_name: The whole Refrigeration or Air-Conditioning Work Law 5785-2025 (63 sections, four schedules) as one L4 module, with Hebrew source comments
licence_note: No licence statement from the contributor is recorded in this row; see the repository NOTICE.

language.note: Identifiers and keywords are English; the source citations and explanatory comments are Hebrew. The package's own notes (README-he.md, coverage-he.md) are Hebrew.

scope: The Law only: all 63 sections and the four schedules (28 First Schedule works, 17 Second Schedule rows in 19 alternatives, 7 Third Schedule violations, and a Fourth Schedule list of 91 refrigerants, see known_issues). NOT covered: the Fees Regulations, their vintages, and the SimpLEX test table, so none of the scenarios in the sibling rows' fee tests can be run against this row.
method: Produced with ChatGPT, without Legalese's encoding-a-subject skill or pipeline. The package's own validation.json records 107 assertions, all passing; they were written by the same run that wrote the code, with no independent test author.
known_issues_as_of_2026-10-13: The Fourth Schedule list has 91 refrigerants; the gazette (Sefer HaChukim 3349) and the current Hebrew Wikisource text list 95. Items (92)-(95), 488A, 489A, 490A and 491A, are missing, so `refrigerant appears in schedule four` answers FALSE for them.

Three periods end one day early against Interpretation Law s.10(b), which puts the last day of a period of years on the day whose number is the event day's and counts that day as INSIDE the period (checked against the enacted official text): `experience transition is open` (hvac-act.l4:591) closes the Second Schedule's three-year window on 2028-07-15 instead of 2028-07-16, and `ordinary repeat violation` (line 1635) and `repeat after warning` (line 1800) exclude the second anniversary with `LESS THAN`, where s.45(b) and s.54(b) say 'within two years'.

The row does not model Interpretation Law s.10(c): rest, recess and holiday days that are the last days of a period are not counted, so a period ending on one runs on to the next day that is not. None of its deadlines takes a calendar.

not_reviewed.note: No review by a domain expert is recorded for this row. A model review on 2026-10-13 compared ss.6, 8, 9, 16, 17, 41-54 and 63, and the Second, Third and Fourth Schedules, with the Hebrew; it did not read the other sections line by line.
